(r − k) × m ÷ (b × 1,000) multiplies by the bottle volume instead of dividing and adds the irrelevant b (two slips), while (r × b) ÷ (k × m × 1,000) and (r × m × 1,000) ÷ (b × k) are three-slip formulas matching the source's two formula fillers exactly.

B over-reads Parcelo's higher margin as more profit, C over-reads Swiftbox's higher fuel share as a higher diesel price, and D (parcel prices) is the one statement without basis that sourceHas allows; comparing total diesel without dividing by vans lands on A, which matches the source's named slip (totals not divided per unit).

d/(k×f) divides by the price instead of multiplying, d×k×f multiplies by fuel economy instead of dividing (as if k were litres per km), and (d×k)/f makes both inversions; each is one or two slips, and no slip gives (d×f)/k.
